![Rachel Vanni for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2025/07/22/multimedia/kd-mississippi-chicken-hqpk/kd-mississippi-chicken-hqpk-threeByTwoMediumAt2X.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp)

This is a pressure cooker version of an easy slow-cooker dinner.
The original is [here](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1027090-mississippi-chicken).

- 1 yellow onion, diced
- 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken. Thighs or breasts or a mix.
Even better would be bone-in breasts, for extra flavour and gelatin.
- 16 whole pepperoncini, stemmed and halved, plus 1/2 cup liquid from the jar
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 3/4 cup unsalted butter, cut into tablespoons
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, minced 
- 2 teaspoons minced fresh chives
- 2 teaspoons minced fresh dill

---

1. Put everything except the fresh herbs in the pressure cooker.

2. Seal and cook on high for 30 minutes.

3. Allow pressure to release naturally. Then uncover. If it is more liquidy
than desired, stir in a few tablespoons of corn starch or a mix of flour and
cooking liquid.

4. Stir in fresh herbs.

5. Serve with rice or garlic bread and a green vegetable.
